haavara . . . What is it?

The Haavara Agreement was an agreement signed in 1933 between the Nazi government of Germany and a German zionist organization that allowed Jews wanting to leave Germany to take a portion of their assets with them if they moved to what was then British Mandate Palestine.

Part of the deal was that only German-made goods could be taken with the emigrants.

To understand the entire story would take a thread pages long, but in short, zionists were mostly communists who hated fascists, but wanted to get Jews to move to Palestine. The nazis hated Jews, and zionists most of all because they were both Jewish and communist, but the German government was trying to recover from the financial collapse of the 1920 that had been engineered by the Versailles treaty that ended WW1.

So the agreement let both sides get something they wanted. the zionists got a deal that encouraged people to move to "Zion" which is what they considered Palestine to be, and let people move enough assets when they emigrated so that they could make a new start (the German government had been increasingly seizing all the assets of people who were trying to flee the country, and those people arrived in their new countries destitute.)

The German government was wanting to stop a boycott of German-made goods that was brewing in neighboring countries, and signing the agreement seemed to work, the boycott fizzed out.

Since part of the emigrants's assets were still seized and the emigrants had to buy German stuff to ship to Palestine, it generated revenues for the government and promoted German industry, which promoted economic recovery. And the nazis got the result they wanted, which was less Jews in Germany.

So basically it was a pragmatic treaty between two mutually hostile organizations that got what both sides wanted. The nazis got more Jews leaving the country, and economic development too, and in return they incentivized the Jews by letting them keep more of their stuff.

But it triggered a furious reaction, both among other zionist organizations and within the German zionist federation, who claimed it was sellout to make any kind of agreement with the nazis. The zionist federation lost many members, and the American zionist organizations went on a major campaign against the Germans because of the treaty.

It also triggered a furious reaction among nazi party members, who claimed it was a sellout, but Adolph Hitler himself as chancellor laid down the law that the agreement was going to stay in place. And it did until Britain declared war on Germany in 1939 and British Palestine became enemy territory.
